title: Sell Mineral Rights in Aneth, UT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Aneth, UT | San Juan County
metaDescription: Own minerals tied to the historic Aneth Field in San Juan County, Utah? We buy Paradox Basin interests directly, with title confirmed before any offer.
heroLead: Aneth gave its name to one of the oldest and largest producing fields in the Paradox Basin, and it sits within the Navajo Nation's boundary in southern San Juan County.
intro: The Aneth Field has produced from Mississippian-age carbonate reservoirs since the 1950s, making it one of the longest-running oil fields in Utah, and it lies almost entirely within the Navajo Nation, which shapes how mineral ownership and leasing work here in ways that differ from the rest of the Paradox Basin further north. Privately held fee mineral interests near Aneth exist alongside tribal trust and allotted minerals, and knowing which category your interest falls into is the necessary first step before anything else.

We buy privately held fee mineral and royalty interests tied to the Aneth Field. Tribal trust and Navajo Nation allotment interests follow a separate process through the Bureau of Indian Affairs that we do not handle, and we will confirm your status honestly before quoting anything.

sections.heading: A long-producing carbonate field
paragraphs: Aneth's reservoir is a Mississippian carbonate rather than the Green River shale that dominates the Uinta Basin further north, and it has been produced by successive operators, including major companies in earlier decades, since the field's discovery. That long history means there is an unusually deep well of production data available for interests here, which we use directly when building a reserve estimate rather than relying on assumptions.

sections.heading: Ownership status comes first
paragraphs: Because so much of the acreage around Aneth sits within Navajo Nation trust boundaries, we confirm ownership status before discussing any number. If your family's interest is fee simple — held outside trust status, sometimes originating from historical non-tribal land transactions in the area — we can typically proceed with a direct purchase. If it is tribal trust or allotted land, that transfers through the BIA, not through us.

faqs.question: Is all mineral ownership near Aneth tribal trust land?
faqs.answer: No, there are privately held fee mineral interests in the area as well. We confirm which category your interest falls into before proceeding.

faqs.question: How long has the Aneth Field been producing?
faqs.answer: Since the 1950s, which gives us an unusually long production history to draw on when valuing an interest here.

faqs.question: Do you handle Navajo Nation allotment transfers?
faqs.answer: No, those go through the Bureau of Indian Affairs. We only purchase privately held fee mineral interests.
